project.name: Layer-Aware Post-Quantum Cryptography for Blockchain-Based Energy Trading
project.authority_rule: Later direct professor clarification overrides the student specification only for the clarified point; the proposal is background and lower authority.
project.measurement_principle: Measure and retain what the system actually does; do not tune results to an expected model.

canonical_e0_server_environment.provenance_note: Historical environment for the retained canonical E0 server run; current host versions must not overwrite it without an E0 rerun.

current_host_observation.provenance_note: Inventory only; these values are not retroactively attributed to retained measurements.

e0_benchmark.status: canonical server data retained; meter/SBC data missing

e1_benchmark.status: functional for all four identity configurations; fixed-profile candidate data retained for ECDSA/ML-DSA-44/ML-DSA-65; SPHINCS+ fixed-profile saturation/failure retained; final E1 CSV incomplete

identity_bytes.aggregation: arithmetic mean of the four peer public-key byte counts; min and max are retained
identity_bytes.dispersion_review_rule: Flag (but do not exclude) a configuration when 100*(max-min)/mean exceeds 3.0 percent.

ECDSA.representation: DER-encoded X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo returned by Fabric ecdsaPublicKey.Bytes() via x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey
ECDSA.provenance: Read-only extraction from the four ECDSA certificates whose SHA-256 values match raw/e1/blockutil-300_ecdsa_identity_bytes.csv; cross-checked against Fabric v2.5.16 bccsp/sw/ecdsakey.go.

ML-DSA-44.representation: raw liboqs public key returned by patched Fabric pqPublicKey.Bytes() and carried in experimental X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.3.9999.1

ML-DSA-65.representation: raw liboqs public key returned by patched Fabric pqPublicKey.Bytes() and carried in experimental X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.3.9999.1

SLH-DSA.representation: raw liboqs public key returned by patched Fabric pqPublicKey.Bytes() and carried in experimental X.509 extension 1.3.6.1.3.9999.1

hybrid_pq_identity.description: Experimental hybrid Fabric identity mechanism: ECDSA X.509 membership and CA chain, a noncritical extension carrying the PQ algorithm and public key, and real liboqs-based peer transaction/endorsement signing and verification.
hybrid_pq_identity.orderer_binary_note: Patched to verify requests signed by PQ peer identities

same_ledger_evidence.closure_classification: mixed: 60 PreferredMaxBytes-driven blocks and 30 BatchTimeout-driven residual blocks; no MaxMessageCount-driven blocks

sphincs_blockutil_54.purpose: Test only whether unchanged Fabric parameters produce a clean traffic-volume-driven ordinary-block population; not a tps_sustained or normal-latency run.

sphincs_low_rate_sweep.reason: Supplemental sustainable-rate characterization after scientifically reportable saturation under the unchanged common 50 TPS workload.
sphincs_low_rate_sweep.sample_count_note: At low rates, 60-second rounds intentionally yield fewer than 1000 requests. The later professor-specified duration is the topic-specific authority for this sweep and must be disclosed.
sphincs_low_rate_sweep.refinement_status: not_needed because 20 TPS passed all sustainability gates
sphincs_low_rate_sweep.final_boundary_status: integer boundary search complete: 22 TPS is the highest tested sustainable integer rate and 23 TPS is the first tested nonsustainable integer rate

transaction_evidence_20_tps.status: transaction-size and endorsement evidence accepted; block utilisation diagnostic-only because closure was BatchTimeout-driven
transaction_evidence_20_tps.closure_interpretation: BatchTimeout-driven: 30 blocks over about 60 seconds matches the 2-second BatchTimeout, 29 nonterminal blocks contain 35-46 transactions around the 40 expected at 20 TPS, and no block approaches MaxMessageCount=500 or PreferredMaxBytes.
transaction_evidence_20_tps.validation_metadata: Unavailable for all 1201 envelopes because peer channel fetch obtained the orderer's block copy, which does not carry peer-added TRANSACTIONS_FILTER metadata. The legacy raw summary grouped unavailable with invalid; the analyzer reports valid=0, invalid=0, unavailable=1201 without modifying raw evidence.

latency_professor_review.population_rule: 50-TPS and 200-TPS populations are separate and are never merged
latency_professor_review.candidate_caveat: ECDSA, ML-DSA-44, and ML-DSA-65 have zero failures and validated timing counts/source hashes, but their historical run logs predate full standardized CPU-preflight capture in-log.
latency_professor_review.sphincs_handling: Common-profile success/error outcomes and Gateway saturation are retained at 50 and 200 TPS; latency fields are intentionally empty and are not normal latency candidates.

caliper.end_to_end_timing_boundary: immediately before proposal.endorse() through successful commit status or the caught failure

sustainability.successful_throughput_definition: Caliper success count divided by the configured 60-second round duration; Caliper displayed throughput is retained but is not used because it can include failed completions.
sustainability.latency_population: successful end-to-end transaction samples ordered by monotonic request-start offset
sustainability.beginning_window: start offsets in [0,12000) ms, the first 20 percent of a 60-second round
sustainability.ending_window: start offsets in [48000,60000) ms, the last 20 percent of a 60-second round
sustainability.final_sphincs_rule: highest tested low-rate sweep point passing all three criteria

endorsement_policy.chaincode_definition_policy: /Channel/Application/Endorsement (Fabric lifecycle default because setup_fabric_e1.sh supplies neither --signature-policy nor --channel-config-policy)
endorsement_policy.configured_interpretation: MAJORITY of two organization Endorsement subpolicies requires one peer endorsement from each organization.
endorsement_policy.generated_channel_artifact_verification: Read-only configtxlator decode of the current generated energychannel.block showed Application Endorsement = ImplicitMeta MAJORITY and each Org1MSP/Org2MSP Endorsement subpolicy = 1-of-1 peer.
endorsement_policy.actual_serialized_count_check: Future block evidence records the endorsement count in every serialized endorser transaction and reports mean/min/max; current retained block CSV predates envelope extraction.

cpu_control.note: Required future-run state; each retained run log records the observed per-CPU values.

fabric_block_parameters.effective_value_source: Decoded generated/current Fabric common.Block config with configtxlator; configtx.yaml is the declarative source.

block_utilisation.definition: mean(actual ordinary-transaction block bytes) / effective PreferredMaxBytes
block_utilisation.scientific_condition: Exclude genesis/config/other blocks; retain terminal ordinary partial blocks. The observed steady-state population must not be BatchTimeout-driven.
block_utilisation.diagnostic_rate_status: 300 TPS was a block-filling probe only. Its block evidence is accepted for block utilisation; Gateway concurrency-limit failures make the run invalid for final latency or tps_sustained.
block_utilisation.observed_closure: Documented empirical observation: blocks 17-47 each contain MaxMessageCount=500 ordinary transactions, demonstrating steady-state count-limit closure rather than BatchTimeout closure. Block 48 is a terminal 386-transaction ordinary block retained in the accepted population.

working_result.population_rule: Exclude genesis/config/other blocks and retain every ordinary transaction block in the measured interval, including the terminal partial block.

full_500_transaction_block_diagnostic_co.status: diagnostic comparison only; does not replace the accepted boundary-inclusive result

block_utilisation.transaction_size_method: For each fetched serialized common.Block, decode protobuf Block.Data.Data[i] as the exact common.Envelope bytes. Record len(Data[i]), SHA-256, transaction ID, validation code, and endorsement count per transaction. tx_bytes_mean is the arithmetic mean of these exact envelope lengths for endorser transactions in accepted ordinary blocks; it is never estimated as block bytes divided by transaction count.
block_utilisation.tx_bytes_status: ECDSA, ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and SPHINCS+ all have accepted exact-envelope and empirical endorsement evidence. The timeout-driven 50-TPS block populations remain diagnostic-only; the older ECDSA block-filling CSV remains the separate accepted block-utilisation source.

ecdsa_transaction_evidence.status: validated_transaction_size_and_endorsement_evidence; block utilisation diagnostic-only because closure was BatchTimeout-driven
ecdsa_transaction_evidence.population: unchanged common-profile warm-up followed by the unchanged 120-second 50-TPS round; the 200-TPS round is omitted
ecdsa_transaction_evidence.reason: The historical ECDSA block evidence contains no serialized envelopes. The standard 50-TPS population yields about 6001 transactions, preserves the common workload payload sequence, avoids congestion, and does not depend on the unresolved final latency-population choice.
ecdsa_transaction_evidence.latency_use: evidence-only; must not replace the retained historical latency candidate
ecdsa_transaction_evidence.closure_interpretation: BatchTimeout-driven: 60 ordinary blocks over the 120-second round matches BatchTimeout=2s; 59 nonterminal blocks contain 100-102 transactions and the terminal residual contains 36, with no block approaching MaxMessageCount=500.
ecdsa_transaction_evidence.validation_evidence: valid=0, invalid=0, unavailable=6001 because the orderer-sourced block copy has no peer-added TRANSACTIONS_FILTER metadata; unavailable is not invalid and does not affect envelope lengths or embedded endorsement counts.
